newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares inch higher as optimism returns.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares inch higher as optimism returns.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.32 percent on Thursday amid signs of increased political stability in the country, and traders said advances were set to continue in the short term.
"Investors have returned, mostly buying shares in companies like Lek, Droga and SKB banka, and that has pulled the market up," said Milos Obed, a trader at bank "A".

Ljubljana shares were boosted more than one percent on Wednesday after the election of Janez Podobnik of the People's Party to the post of parliamentary president, which was widely considered as a sign of political stabilisation after an inconclusive general election on November 10.
* The 10-share SBI index rose 3.76 points to 1,183.7.
* Drug maker Lek's issue A shares were the most actively traded, firming 1.01 percent to 19,950 tolars on volume of 2,055 shares.
* Overall 15 shares rose, one fell and one was unchanged, while eight were untraded.
